title: pod-start-stall-node-diskpressure-cni-heartbeat-notes
content:
Summary:
Node(s) intermittently reported DiskPressure which coincided with pods stuck in ContainerCreating / ImagePullBackOff and CNI heartbeat timeouts. Pod creation stalled for ~30-90s; kube-scheduler retried and overall latency for small control-plane jobs spiked. Impact: intermittent ingestion and test harness jobs failing; overall user-facing hosted API not impacted but internal pipelines degraded.

Top-level hypothesis:
- Persistent writers on nodes were saturating local ephemeral-storage leading to kernel reclaim and kubelet marking nodes DiskPressure.
- Kubelet eviction and cgroup interactions blocked container runtime tasks (image unpack, container start).
- CNI agent (weave/ovn/flannel - environment had calico-vxlan) lost periodic heartbeats due to transient high CPU/io on host; this surfaced as network attach timeouts during pod creation.
- Root cause likely a memory leak in an infra sidecar (log-forwarder) + unexpected logrotate behavior writing into /var/lib/kubelet or /var/lib/containerd overlay -> premature disk fill.

Timeline (local times, approx):
- 2025-11-02 03:12 UTC: Alert fired - cluster: node-az3a-014 DiskPressure (kubelet).
- 03:12-03:14: Several pods submitted by CI queued in ContainerCreating. kubectl describe showed "failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded".
- 03:14: Observed heavy dstat i/o wait and journalctl shows repeated log-forwarder OOMKilled on same host.
- 03:16: Manual drain attempted (kubectl drain node-az3a-014 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data). Drain hung when trying to evict pods in ContainerCreating state.
- 03:20: Restarted CRI: systemctl restart containerd -> short improvement in container start latency but DiskPressure reappeared within 5m.
- 03:27: Restarted kubelet (systemctl restart kubelet) on node -> CNI agent reconnected; however kubelet again reported DiskPressure within 10m.
- 03:35: Identified log-forwarder writing to /var/lib/kubelet/plugins/csi rather than /var/log (misconfigured path in new systemd unit).
- 03:50: Reconfigured unit and rotated logs; freed ~18GB on node. DiskPressure cleared. Pod creation returned to normal by 04:00.

Commands used and useful quick checks (notes to self):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide
- kubectl describe node <node> | egrep -A3 "Conditions|Non-terminated Pods"
- kubectl get pods --all-namespaces | grep ContainerCreating
- journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager
- journalctl -u containerd -n 200 --no-pager
- sudo du -sh /var/lib/kubelet/* /var/lib/containerd/* | sort -h | tail -n 20
- ss -lnp | grep vxlan  # check CNI vxlan ports
- crictl ps -a; crictl logs <sandbox-pid>

Intermediate mitigations taken during incident:
- Set taint node with key temporary-maintenance=true: kubectl taint nodes node-az3a-014 temporary-maintenance=true:NoSchedule to stop new scheduling while investigating.
- Restarted containerd and kubelet to clear stuck RPCs.
- Forced log rotation on log-forwarder service and moved current log file to /var/log/infra-logs/ to free space.
- Increased kubelet eviction threshold for ephemeral-storage temporarily to avoid repeated flapping while cleanup finishes (not ideal, noted as temporary band-aid).

Observed metrics and signals that correlated with downtime:
- inode usage on /var/lib/kubelet spiked before overall capacity reached 100% -> suggests many small files (checkpoint/cache)
- /proc/pressure/io showed increased stall times (~15ms->120ms spikes).
- CNI agent heartbeat interval jitter increased from normal ~5s to 40-60s during the worst period.
- kubelet logs: repeated "eviction manager: attempt reclaim ..." followed by "NodeCondition DiskPressure true".

Root cause analysis (current best understanding):
1) Misconfigured log-forwarder (recent rollout) started writing retained diagnostic dumps into /var/lib/kubelet/plugins/csi (wrong path). Files accumulated (many small files) causing inode and ephemeral-storage pressure.
2) The combination of high i/o and inode exhaustion caused container runtime ops (image unpack, network namespace setup) to block; kubelet marked node DiskPressure and refused scheduling, which cascaded into ContainerCreating hang.
3) While node was under pressure, the CNI agent experienced delayed heartbeats (both due to CPU/io and local socket timeouts), and network attach calls hit deadlines -> additional pod startup failures.

Longer-term fixes and action items (owner / ETA):
- [Owner: Samir Khan] Fix log-forwarder systemd unit to write to /var/log/infra/ and add a logrotate conf that keeps < 1GB per host. ETA: 2025-11-07.
- [Owner: Elena Park] Add alert for inode pressure on ephemeral-storage mounts (not just disk usage) and surface in SRE dashboard. ETA: 2025-11-10.
- [Owner: Noah Friedman] Audit recent rollouts to systemd units that touch /var/lib paths; add preflight check script for path validation. ETA: 2025-11-09.
- [Owner: eng-sre] Create a short emergency runbook for DiskPressure during pod creation stalls (steps to taint/drain vs restart kubelet/cri). Draft below. ETA: 2025-11-12.

Draft emergency runbook (first cut):
Purpose: fast steps to recover node where pods stuck in ContainerCreating due to DiskPressure/CNI timeouts.
1) Confirm node condition: kubectl describe node <node> | grep -A2 Conditions
2) If DiskPressure true: inspect local storage quickly: sudo du -sh /var/lib/kubelet/* | sort -h | tail -n 10 and sudo ls -lah /var/lib/kubelet/plugins/csi | head -n 20
3) If a misbehaving service is writing to kubelet paths: systemctl stop <service> && mv /var/lib/kubelet/plugins/csi/<big_files> /var/log/infra-temp/ && systemctl restart <service>
4) If pods are stuck and drain will hang: kubectl taint nodes <node> temporary-maintenance=true:NoSchedule (so scheduler stops sending new pods).
5) Restart container runtime: sudo systemctl restart containerd (watch crictl ps). If still stuck after 60s then restart kubelet: sudo systemctl restart kubelet.
6) Monitor kubelet/journal and CNI logs for reconnection: journalctl -u kubelet -f and kubectl get pods -o wide | grep ContainerCreating
7) Re-enable scheduling after cleanup: kubectl taint nodes <node> temporary-maintenance:NoSchedule-
8) Post-incident: ensure logs moved, run du -sh to confirm freed, and open follow-up ticket for a permanent fix.

Open questions / follow-ups for postmortem:
- Why did log-forwarder path change get through deploy without a preflight check? (CI job gap?)
- Did the kubelet eviction thresholds need to be tuned for our workload patterns, or is this purely a path/config bug?
- Should we add periodic inode checks for /var/lib/kubelet and containerd directories?
- Can we add a small admission-controller check to prevent pods/daemonsets from creating massive numbers of tiny files into kubelet-managed paths?

Notes and tangential observations:
- We saw two nodes with the same symptom in different AZs but only one had the misconfigured forwarder; the other had a burst of kubelet image pull caches during a CI wave -> suggests two independent vectors can converge to same failure mode.
- There is some similarity to previous "swapfile scheduler backpressure" incident (ref internal notes) but this time inode pressures mattered more than raw disk bytes.
- Quick idea: add a lightweight systemd tmpfiles.d rule to cap number of files in /var/lib/kubelet/plugins/csi for safety.

Immediate next steps after today's notes:
- Convert this draft into a short post-incident doc with timeline + RCA and circulate to infra-eng and release teams.
- Implement log-forwarder config fix and schedule hotfix deployment to other nodes (Samir).
- Add inode alert and update runbook (Elena).

Appendix: useful log excerpts (sanitized)
- kubelet: "eviction manager: reclaiming ephemeral-storage, node condition DiskPressure = true"
- containerd: "failed to create containerd task: context deadline exceeded"
- system: "log-forwarder[4521]: writing diagnostic dump to /var/lib/kubelet/plugins/csi/dump-2025-11-02-0304-*.tgz"

-- end of on-call note draft.

(Notes to self: turn the above into a short runbook in Confluence; attach the crontab for log rotation and link the JIRA SRE-1423.)
